d.d: Any member of a race of beings from (especially Scandinavian and other Germanic) folklore, usually depicted as having some sort of supernatural powers and being skilled in crafting and metalworking, often as short with long beards, and sometimes as clashing with elves.
An animal, plant or other thing much smaller than the usual of its sort.

d.x: The specimen is a very dwarf form of the plant.

d.d: To render (much) smaller, turn into a dwarf (version).
To make appear (much) smaller, puny, tiny; to be much larger than.
d.x: The newly-built skyscraper dwarfs all older buildings in the downtown skyline.

d.d: simple past and past participle of dwarf
present participle and gerund of dwarf
The situation where something is made to seem (relatively) small or unimportant.
The condition of being a dwarf (person of short stature).
The quality of being puny or inferior.
third-person singular simple present indicative of dwarf
Similar to a dwarf, for example in stature.
Of, pertaining to, or made by or for dwarfs/dwarves.
